'''''Pleioblastus''''' is an [[East Asia]]n [[genus]] of [[monopodial]] [[bamboo]]s in the [[Poaceae|grass family]] Poaceae.<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/8367863#page/407/mode/1up Nakai, Takenoshin. 1925.  Journal of the Arnold Arboretum 6(3): 145–147] descriptions in Latin, commentary in English</ref><ref name="Ohrnberger">{{cite book | last = Ohrnberger | first = D. | title = The Bamboos of the World | publisher = Elsevier Science | year = 1999 | pages = 596 | isbn = 978-0-444-50020-5}}</ref> They are [[native plant|native]] to [[China]] and [[Japan]], and naturalized in scattered places in [[Korea]], [[Europe]], [[New Zealand]], and the [[Western Hemisphere]].<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=125899 Flora of China Vol. 22 Page 121 <big>苦竹属</big> ku zhu shu ''Pleioblastus'' Nakai, J. Arnold Arbor. 6: 145. 1925]</ref>

The plant spreads by vigorous underground [[rhizomes]] which run along just beneath the soil surface, producing plantlets at the nodes.  These can be used to [[Plant propagation|propagate]] new plants, but if not removed they can become invasive.

The species ''[[Pleioblastus variegatus]]''<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector – ''Pleioblastus variegatus''|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=1497|accessdate=28 May 2013}}</ref> (green and cream stripes), and ''P. viridistriatus''<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector – ''Pleioblastus viridistriatus''|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=1493|accessdate=28 May 2013}}</ref> (green and yellow stripes) have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name="RHSAZ"/><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants – Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 80 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 7 May 2018}}</ref> 

Genetic research suggests that this genus may properly be part of the genus ''[[Arundinaria]]''.<ref name="Zhuge">{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1007/BF02856844 | last = Zhuge | first = Qiang |author2=Yu-long Ding |author3=Chen Xu |author4=Hui-yu Zou |author5=Min-ren Huang |author6=Ming-xiu Wang | title = A preliminary analysis of phylogenetic relationships of ''Arundinaria'' and related genera based on nucleotide sequences of nrDNA (ITS region) and cpDNA (trnL-F intergenic spacer) | journal = Journal of Forestry Research | publisher = Springer | volume = 16 | issue = 1 | pages = 5–8 | year = 2005 | s2cid = 23456979 }}</ref>
